name: עַזְגָּד
gloss: Gad is strong; or fortune is strong
summary: The head of a large family that returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezr 2:12; Neh 7:17), of whom more came with Ezra (Ezr 8:12); and one who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day (Neh 10:16), perhaps the family's head of that time. The name is עַז “strong” with גָּד, “fortune” (Gen 30:11) or Gad, the god of fortune whom Isaiah rebukes (Isa 65:11); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The sons of עַזְגָּד, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two.”
“Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan.”
“Bunni, עַזְגָּד, Bebai”, among the heads who sealed.

note: BDB's p.bx.as, four tokens. TIPNR's Azgad@Neh.10.15 is Neh 10:16 in the Hebrew numbering. Phoenician names of the same shape (ʿzbʿl, ʿzmlk: a god's name after עז) are the comparison. Whether גָּד is the god or “fortune” is not shown.
